$schema-note: EngiRent single source of truth for design tokens (E3.1). Every value here was DERIVED from the four surfaces' existing theme files on 2026-09-08, not invented — Flutter (core/constants/app_colors.dart, core/theme/*), admin (src/app/theme.ts + src/app/globals.css), kiosk (src/theme.css), website (styles/globals.css). Generators (design/tokens/build.mjs) emit per-surface artifacts FROM this file so the four can no longer drift by hand. References like {palette.teal.500} resolve to the raw ramp value.
$revision: 2 — 2026-09-08. Rev 1 was built from theme.ts alone; rev 2 corrects four values against the surfaces that actually render (see $corrections).

$corrections.$note: Each entry: what rev 1 said, what the repo renders, and where that was read. The repo wins over the doc; these are the four places it did.
$corrections.website-themes: Rev 1 said the website is light-only. It is NOT: client/web/styles/globals.css:50 declares a full `.dark` block, driven by next-themes (app/providers.tsx:3) with a user-facing toggle (components/theme-switch.tsx:22). The website renders BOTH themes. Only the kiosk is single-theme.
$corrections.light-surfaceAlt: Rev 1 took #F3F8F7 from admin theme.ts's `surfaceTokens`, which has ZERO consumers (grep: only its own definition). The value three LIVE consumers render is #EEF4FB — admin globals.css:28 (--color-surface-soft), web globals.css:37 (--brand-soft), Flutter core/widgets/app_widgets.dart:25. Flutter app_theme.dart:43 is the lone #F3F8F7 holdout and the generator unifies it. #F3F8F7 is also green-tinted, a leftover of the pre-mandate teal; #EEF4FB is in the same blue family as border #D5E3F2.
$corrections.dark-accent: Rev 1 resolved dark accent to {palette.gold.300} = #f8c86f, which NO surface renders. All four render #F5B85C — Flutter secondaryOnDark (app_colors.dart:93), kiosk --gold (theme.css:46), admin --color-secondary dark (globals.css:48), web .dark --brand-secondary (globals.css:58). Added to the gold ramp as `onDark`.
$corrections.dark-cta: Same shape: rev 1 said {palette.coral.300} = #fd8797, nothing renders it. All four render #FF8A95 — Flutter accentOnDark (app_colors.dart:94), kiosk --coral (theme.css:50), admin globals.css:49, web globals.css:59. Added to the coral ramp as `onDark`.

$darkStatusRule: Dark-theme status hues lift one ramp step (500 -> 400) ONLY where the 500 fails to clear 6:1 against the dark ground #050F1A; otherwise the 500 stands. Measured by design/tokens/verify.mjs: success #22C55E 8.46:1 (stays), warning #F59E0B 8.97:1 (stays), critical #EF4444 5.12:1 (lifts to #F37373, 6.89:1), review #0E9BB8 5.87:1 (lifts to #33B6D1, 8.03:1). The critical lift is not invented — admin globals.css:50 already renders #f37373 on dark; the rule generalises what the repo had done by hand for one colour.
$fillVsInk: THE RULE THAT MAKES STATUS COLOUR ACCESSIBLE, and the one the four surfaces currently break. A status ramp's 500 is a FILL/identity hue — a chip ground, a bar, a dot, a locker tile. It is NOT a text colour on a light surface: measured on #FFFFFF, success #22C55E is 2.28:1, warning #F59E0B 2.15:1, accent #E9A13B 2.18:1, cta #EF6E7B 2.92:1 — all under the 4.5:1 body floor and most under even the 3:1 graphic floor. So every family also resolves an `<role>Ink` for on-light text and icons, at the lowest ramp step that clears 4.5:1 against BOTH #FFFFFF and its own 50 fill. Steps were computed, not chosen: emerald 800, warn 900, danger 700, review 700, gold 900, coral 800, teal 500. On DARK the lifted hues already clear 6:1 as text, so `<role>Ink` resolves to the role itself there.
$borderRule: Two border roles, because WCAG 1.4.11 applies to one and not the other. `border` is the decorative hairline that separates a card from its ground — the mandate's 'borders do the work shadows used to' — and carries no contrast floor. `borderStrong` is the visible boundary of an interactive control (a text input's enabled outline, an unchecked checkbox), which 1.4.11 requires at 3:1. The current #D5E3F2 is 1.30:1 on white and is used for BOTH, so every text input in the product currently fails 1.4.11. Measured replacements that clear 3:1 on both of their theme's grounds: light #6E8FB3 (3.36 / 3.19), dark #43708F (3.63 / 3.31).

palette.$note: Raw, theme-agnostic ramps. 500 is the on-light anchor; higher = darker, lower = lighter. `onDark` is the hue's dark-ground anchor where the surfaces render a specific lifted value rather than a ramp step. These match Flutter AppColors and admin's Mantine tuples to the hex today.

teal.$note: Brand. Despite the name (kept because admin's Mantine tuple is literally called `teal` and renaming it churns every color prop) this ramp is blue — #0B5FA5.

review.$note: The PENDING / under-review family. Cyan-teal DISTINCT from brand blue, seeded from Flutter's existing info #0E9BB8. Promoted cross-surface by E3.1 to satisfy 'PENDING is never red or warning-yellow'. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by the human: pending-family statuses use this cyan (NOT brand blue, NOT the old warning-yellow). CONTRAST CAVEAT: #0E9BB8 is 3.11:1 on the light ground — fine as a chip fill or 3:1 UI border, BELOW the 4.5:1 floor as body text. On light, pending chips use the 50 fill + 700 ink pairing (5.25:1), never 500-on-white text.

ink.$note: Neutral ramp, TEAL/BLUE-TINTED on purpose — the mandate bans the generic #6B7280 gray family. Flutter still uses banned greys (#9CA3AF/#4B5563/#D1D5DB/#F3F4F6/#1F2937); E3.1 replaces them with these.

semantic.$note: Role tokens, resolved per theme. Screens consume these, never a raw ramp value.

statusChip.$note: How a status chip resolves, so 'one meaning everywhere' is a rule the generators emit rather than a convention each surface re-invents. On light: a tinted 50 fill with the family's Ink step as text — a flat 700 does NOT work for every ramp (emerald 700 is 3.51:1 on its own fill, warn 700 is 3.09:1), so the ink step is per-family and was computed, not picked. On dark: the role hue at 14% over the surface, with the role itself as text — the lifted dark hues all clear 6:1 so they need no separate ink.

status.$note: Domain status -> semantic role. ONE meaning across all four surfaces. The vocabulary is DERIVED from server/node_server/prisma/schema.prisma, which is the authority: RentalStatus, TransactionStatus, VerificationDecision and VerificationStatus, plus the handful of non-enum states the UIs render (OVERDUE, ONLINE/OFFLINE, the ID-verification states from E2.4). Note that COMPLETED appears in THREE enums and PENDING in all four — which is precisely why one meaning has to be settled here rather than per page.
status.$e31Change: Today Flutter and admin both map the pending family to warning (yellow). This table moves it to 'review' (cyan #0E9BB8), the human's 2026-09-08 ruling. Two smaller unifications ride along: COMPLETED was brand-blue in admin and is now success, and VERIFICATION was coral (the CTA colour, which should never carry a status) and is now review.
status.$accentNote: DEPOSITED and REFUNDED stay on the gold accent rather than collapsing into success. Both mean 'money moved and is being held', which is a distinct milestone from 'this rental is fine' — and admin already drew that distinction. Preserving it is a smaller and more honest change than flattening it.

space.$grid: 8px, with a single 4px sub-step for icon-label gaps only

elevation.$note: borders do the work shadows used to — one hairline shadow, no ladder

interaction.$note: E3.1 bullet 5, added 2026-09-09. Before this there was NOT ONE :focus-visible rule in the repo -- measured, not assumed: tabbing the website gave every control the browser default `outline: auto 1px`, whose computed colour in DARK mode is rgb(16,16,16) on a near-black ground. Frameworks were carrying focus for admin (Mantine) and Flutter (Material); the website and kiosk had nothing of their own. focusRing.role is `brand` because it clears 3:1 against the page ground in BOTH resolutions by a wide margin (6.23:1 light, 7.08:1 dark), which WCAG 1.4.11 requires of a focus indicator exactly as it does of a control border.
interaction.$hoverNote: kiosk.hover is false -- it is a touch panel with no pointer, and screens.css correctly contains zero :hover rules. Generators must NOT emit a hover overlay for the kiosk.

kiosk.$note: The kiosk renders the DARK resolution only (theme.css --bg #050f1a) and is the ONLY single-theme surface. Physical corridor-lighting contrast check is B-2-blocked while the Pi is offline.
kiosk.$typeNote: typeScaleMultiplier had NO CONSUMER and nothing to multiply until 2026-09-09: scale/ defines space, radius, motion and elevation but no type scale, and the kiosk's steps were hand-authored in theme.css. typeBase below is those authored values, moved here unchanged, so the multiplier finally applies to something. Each entry is [minPx, vmin, maxPx] for a clamp(); the generator multiplies all three by typeScaleMultiplier. 1vmin on a 1080x1920 panel is 10.8px. Measured before applying it: body copy rendered 17.3px and the smallest step 13.5px on the real panel, which is too small for a wall-mounted display read standing at arm's length.
